sources.entry: Tincta - One-window text editor with syntax highlighting.

summary.one_liner: Tincta is a free, one-window native macOS text editor with syntax highlighting, published as source by its makers after they stopped maintaining the app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Tincta as a free Mac text editor focused on speed, stability and ease of use. Listed features include syntax coloring for over 65 languages, search and replace with RegEx support, line numbering, full Unicode support, and built-in and custom color themes. Smaller features include auto-close brackets, auto-indent, a page guide, line wrapping, drag and drop, block selection, a spell checker, printing, invisible-character display, encoding conversion, line-ending conversion, and tab/space conversion. The README also says the source is kept on GitHub as a reference for anyone who wants to build it themselves. It should compile with Xcode, but the project includes the maintainers' dev certificate, which must be removed or replaced, and the App Store build references a Sentry crash reporter whose config file is not included.
use_cases: edit source code with syntax highlighting on a Mac
search and replace text using regular expressions
convert line endings or text encodings
convert tabs to spaces in a text file
use a lightweight one-window text editor on macOS
study or build a native macOS Cocoa text editor
how_to_run: Remove or replace the dev certificate set up in the project
Optionally create SentryConfig.h from SentryConfig_Example.h, or remove Sentry references and the import from Tincta-AppStore-Prefix.pch
notable: Originally started in 2011, built for Snow Leopard
Source kept public as a reference after the app was pulled from the App Store
caveats: No longer available in the App Store because it does not work reliably on macOS Ventura and later
Maintainers no longer actively develop it; the codebase is over 10 years old
Build requires removing the maintainers' dev certificate and handling the Sentry config
